clauses.reason: Keep confidence at public boundaries and execution under one owner.

updates.rationale: Repeated labels, frontend matrices and nested lifecycle setup multiply cost without proportionate confidence.
scope: Product tests and agent testing instructions
updates.statement: Each distinct public contract keeps necessary real traversal; core matrices execute once and portable and installed boundaries retain representative independent execution.

updates.rationale: Independent runner commands and repeated member tests duplicate work and let execution policy drift.
updates.statement: Explicit diagnostic targets, readiness and CI share supervised execution and resource allocation. Admission and conflict continuation prepare and run static checks only; final remains complete.

updates.rationale: Measured resource ownership and reduced work are more reliable than guessed worker widths or additional maintenance ledgers.
updates.statement: Observe actual phase and preparation cost, reuse only successful immutable preparation, and keep one locked static authority without permanent test-count or timing budgets.

decisions.reason: The owner approved the reviewed Perdura alignment and concrete test-consolidation plan.

revision.summary: Preserve behavioral confidence while reducing repeated validation work.

transaction.reason: Apply the owner-approved standalone efficiency decision before implementation.

observations.reason: Change records multiply ordinary intent labels, generated matrices repeat shared algorithms, and broad repository fixtures eagerly provision unused remotes. Largest-child RSS is an OS observation, not a whole-worker process-tree memory estimate.
observations.summary: The pre-change member corpus passes 1724 nodes with four allocated workers; the same-host test shard took 279.93 seconds and 778.49 reported child CPU seconds.

observations.reason: Use one supervised diagnostic owner, bound nested execution, and let complete final validation judge integration. The public lifecycle remains eight operations.
observations.summary: CI invokes pytest independently of the allocator, and conflict continuation repeats member diagnostics before static checks.

observations.reason: Retain one locked Ruff authority and existing hooks for other checks; update current instructions without another workflow ledger.
observations.summary: The pre-commit gate repeats Ruff under a separate pinned version and some nested uv commands can sync again.

transaction.reason: Retain the measured baseline and concrete redundant work before changing the corpus.

observations.reason: The standalone-capacity cases must explicitly isolate their injected host inputs from the enclosing test context. Public diagnostic cases separately prove the nested one-lane bound. The original parallel failures remained failures and published no readiness evidence.
observations.summary: Three pre-existing host-allocation assertions expected two workers while executing inside an enclosing xdist lane; the new policy correctly supplied one. Their serial diagnostic retries passed.

observations.reason: Keep the real parallel first failure and serial diagnostic retry; change only the superseded inner-width expectation. Bound an explicit outer lane even when the enclosing numeric environment is absent, and preserve the original failed command diagnostic.
observations.summary: The existing native pytest allocation/retry test explicitly creates an outer worker but still expected two inner workers; both frontends correctly launched one under the new contract.

observations.reason: Insert owned options before the native separator, preserving literal test paths and the enclosing allocation. Extend the existing real retry traversal rather than add another matrix.
observations.summary: Both native allocation/retry cases failed when a valid pytest end-of-options separator preceded the target path; injected worker and diagnostic flags became filenames.

observations.reason: Direct subprocess fixtures inherited the outer shard allocation. Make nonparallel runner fixtures explicitly serial and preserve explicit parallel scenarios with an observed worker count, without changing gate allocation or verdicts.
observations.summary: All four engine/generated scratch cases observed four child pytest workers even when their declared scenario was serial or two workers.

observations.reason: Terminate Just option parsing before the protocol recipe, including in the standard skill launcher. Keep native arguments literal and validate the actual shortcut plus installed launcher, rather than accepting only direct Python invocation. The new worktree also required ordinary trust of its unchanged declared mise configuration.
observations.summary: The actual just test shortcut lost the native end-of-options separator through nested Just parsing and the protocol parser refused --no-cov.

observations.reason: Preserve the strict committed-binding rule. Commit bindings, append the retained observations through the owned writer, verify applied state and reconcile them before readiness. Guidance now distinguishes a refused request from a recorded event.
observations.summary: Five discovery writes were refused while repository bindings were uncommitted; the requests had not entered source history when independent fixes continued.

transaction.reason: Capture retained execution discoveries after the binding commit; preserve each original observation identity and the earlier no-mutation refusals.

clauses.reason: Preserve the owner direction as individually amendable product principles.

updates.rationale: A protocol that creates more coordination than it removes fails its purpose.
updates.statement: Signetum exists to help development: workflow and review burden, including maintaining the protocol itself, count as product costs.

updates.rationale: Dogfooding exposes installation, command, evidence and maintenance problems that module-only tests can miss.
updates.statement: Signetum develops itself through the shipped protocol and implementation owners; self-use friction is evidence for product repair rather than a reason for a private bypass.

updates.rationale: Actual development failures supply better product requirements than speculative process machinery.
updates.statement: Perdura is an originating application and continuing source of verified development lessons. Absorb and generalize demonstrated problems and useful mechanisms while preserving repository-specific policy boundaries.

updates.rationale: Users need a usable entrypoint and credible outcomes, not unsupported scale or reliability claims.
updates.statement: Keep installation, distribution and use simple through one standard Skill and repository-owned instructions and commands. Position for reliable development with large agent teams using concrete cases and accurately bounded evidence.

decisions.reason: The owner explicitly established development usefulness, dogfooding and Perdura experience as the product foundations, with convenient distribution and evidence-led large-agent-team positioning.

boundaries: Keep repository-specific policy outside the generic protocol.
Marketing claims retain their actual evidence boundary.
revision.summary: Development utility, self-use, originating application experience and easy distribution.

transaction.reason: Apply the owner-directed product principles before updating the current product guidance.
